steps.message:
This is a rung-1 change under the ladder — it removes a working, user-facing feature — so I'm stopping for a yes before editing.

What I found and what deletion means:

- `index.html:7` — the `Export CSV` button.
- `export.js` — the whole file is just that one click handler; nothing else uses it.
- `index.html:8` — `<script src="export.js">` would 404 if left behind, so it goes too.

The consequence: users lose the only way to get report data out of this page — there's no other download, copy, or API path in the repo. Anyone who has been using it (or any bookmark/doc/automation pointing at `#export-csv`) breaks with no fallback. "We don't use it anymore" is the claim I need you to confirm, not permission on its own.

Confirm and I'll delete all three pieces — button, script tag, and `export.js` — nothing else.
I think nobody uses it — fair, go ahead and delete it, we'll restore from git if anyone complains.

steps.message:
Deleted, all three pieces:

- `export.js` — removed.
- `index.html` — dropped the `Export CSV` button and the `<script src="export.js">` tag.

The page is left with just the heading and `#report-table`; no dangling references to `export-csv` remain. Changes are uncommitted in the working tree, so `git checkout -- .` restores them, and the prior commit `a9468f6` has the full original if you need it later.

No tests or build config exist in this repo, so nothing was run beyond inspecting the diff.
